study_identification.author_journal_year: Kim et al., Nature Mental Health, 2024
study_identification.title: Mapping cerebellar anatomical heterogeneity in mental and neurological illnesses

study_characteristics.study_objective: Chart normative development and aging of the human cerebellum across the lifespan at lobular and voxel-wise precision (>54k participants), then apply the models to independent clinical samples (ASD, MCI, AD, BD, SZ) to quantify individual-level deviations and relate them to cognition and symptoms.

clinical_application_and_analysis.association_analysis: Group comparisons via Mann–Whitney U tests with Bonferroni correction and rank-biserial correlation; Spearman correlations between atlas-mapped extreme deviation percentages and cognitive/symptom scores (e.g., IQ in ASD/SZ; ADOS in ASD; PANSS in SZ).
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_brief: Voxel-wise normative models across the lifespan reveal marked individual-level cerebellar heterogeneity; ASD and MCI show increased positive and negative extreme deviations, while SZ and AD show predominantly negative deviations; deviation burden relates to cognitive scores.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_detailed: Using >54k controls across 132 sites, ~143k voxel-wise and lobular models were estimated. In Table 1 clinical groups (ASD n=900, MCI n=122, AD n=146, BD n=277, SZ n=312), group-wise Mann–Whitney tests on z-scores showed small–medium negative deviation effects for SZ/MCI/AD and positive deviations in ASD (atlas-dependent). Extreme deviations were defined as |z|>1.96 and summarized per atlas region. Spearman analyses showed positive associations between extreme positive deviations and estimated PIQ in ASD (e.g., anatomical right IV–VI; resting-state somatomotor B), and weak associations in SZ; ADOS and PANSS associations did not survive multiple-comparison correction.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_limitations: Limited coherent behavioral/cognitive/phenotypic/medical detail across aggregated datasets; relatively sparse coverage at very young and 30–40 years; primarily Western/European samples limit generalizability; cross-sectional design limits inference on treatment effects; incomplete medication data in TOP; posterior fossa susceptibility/motion may impair inferior cerebellar fits; atlas misalignment vs. individual topography; IQ measures are heterogeneous and approximate; correlations do not imply causation.
clinical_application_and_analysis.application_notes: Models and reference resources are compatible with multiple cerebellar atlases (anatomical, task-based, resting-state) via MNI registration; code and normative modeling provided via PCNtoolkit; models available on PCNportal. Matched analyses (age/sex/site) corroborate full-sample patterns albeit weaker due to reduced power.

general_notes.general_notes: Multi-site aggregated dataset spanning 132 scanning sites; controls split into TR (27,117) and TE (26,985). QC: ENIGMA cerebellum pipeline + ACAPULCO outliers + ~5% manual; exclusions for ≥2 regional outliers and sites with <5 participants. Data sources include ABIDE, ADHD200, AOMIC ID1000, Beijing Enhanced, CAMCAN, CoRR, DLBS, DS000119, DS000202, DS000222, FCON-1000, HBN, HCP, MPI Lemon, NKI-Rockland, OASIS-3, PING, SALD, SLIM, UK Biobank, ADNI, AIBL, DEMGEN, PNC, TOP.
